title: The Last Kitchen
premise: Lena Zhou has spent seven years keeping her head down in Maple Hollow, raising her daughter and running the bookshop while quietly nursing the orchard she inherited from her grandmother. When a survey error reveals that half of Willow Orchard legally belongs to Theo Marchetti, the boy who left town with her heart and never came back, the two are forced to negotiate a deed neither will sell. As the autumn festival approaches, Lena must decide whether to protect her found family's claim or admit the truth she's buried: she never stopped loving him. She chooses truth, and they rebuild the orchard, and the bookshop, together.
about_author: Marguerite Joubert is a former pastry chef turned novelist who writes small-town romances from a converted barn in the Hudson Valley. Her work is known for stubborn heroines, second chances, and kitchens that smell like memory.

chapters.title: The Deed in the Drawer
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. While cataloguing her late grandmother's papers for a library exhibit, Lena discovers the survey error: Theo Marchetti holds half of Willow Orchard, the land she's tended for seven years. The emotional beat is quiet dread—her carefully ordered life, built on staying invisible, cracks open the moment his name surfaces.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Lena and Theo. Theo returns to town to claim his inheritance, and their first meeting in the orchard is all old wounds and new frost. His career as a restaurateur is at a crossroads; hers is rooted in Maple Hollow. The beat is wary reconnection—banter that keeps slipping into confession.

chapters.title: Festival of Small Fires
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. During the town's autumn festival, Theo's business partners pressure him to sell the orchard to a developer, and Lena's found family—her daughter June and the bookshop regulars—rally to block it. When Theo overhears Lena call him 'the mistake that saved me,' he nearly signs. The beat is betrayal and rising stakes.

chapters.title: The Last Kitchen
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, converging. At the festival's closing night, Lena chooses truth over loyalty to her own defenses, publicly offering Theo the whole deed—and the whole story of why she never wrote. He tears up the developer's contract, and they cook the festival's last supper together in the orchard kitchen. The beat is surrender: love in the present tense at last.
